mainTopic: Rewards for teaching תורה, sources for תחיית המתים, and a series of רבי אלעזר's sayings on דעה and conduct
overview: The amud opens by finishing a reading of משלי 11:26: whoever holds back תורה from a student is cursed even by unborn babies, or, according to עולא בר ישמעאל, pierced full of holes. The one who does teach receives blessings like יוסף, and רב ששת adds that he will go on teaching in עולם הבא. רבא, רבינא and רב אשי then each bring a פסוק as a source for תחיית המתים. Next comes a long list of sayings by רבי אלעזר. They cover a gentle leader, the greatness of דעה and the מקדש (with a challenge from רב אדא קרחינאה about vengeance), what happens to people without דעה, a house without תורה at night, supporting תלמידי חכמים, leaving bread on the table, going back on one's word, and staying out of the spotlight. Two of these sayings seem to clash about leaving bread over, and the גמרא settles it by whether a whole loaf is present. The גמרא then returns to תחיית המתים: the grave is like a womb, taking in and giving out, and a קל וחומר strengthens the point. The amud ends with the teaching that the צדיקים who are brought back to life will never return to dust.

steps.title: Proving what each word of the verse means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק and proves from other פסוקים that לאום means unborn babies, קבה means a curse, and בר means תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...the nations shall curse him.' And לאום means only unborn babies, as it says: 'And one nation [לאום] shall be stronger than the other nation.' And קבה means only a curse, as it says: 'How can I curse whom God has not cursed [קבה]?' And בר means only תורה, as it says: 'Kiss the בר, lest He be angry.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof already underway. It shows, word by word, that the פסוק ״מֹנֵעַ בָּר יִקְּבֻהוּ לְאוֹם״ means that unborn babies curse whoever holds back תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each key word is defined by pointing to another פסוק where the same word clearly has that meaning. לאום appears in the story of רבקה's pregnancy, so it means babies in the womb. קבה appears in בלעם's words, so it means cursing. בר appears in a פסוק about serving ה׳, so it means תורה. Putting the pieces together: whoever withholds תורה is cursed even by unborn babies.

keyTerms.meaning: Nation; here read as unborn babies
Literally grain; here read as תורה
'X means nothing other than Y': a formula for defining a word

steps.confusionAlert: This text picks up in the middle of a פסוק. The full פסוק is משלי 11:26: ״מֹנֵעַ בָּר יִקְּבֻהוּ לְאוֹם״, 'One who holds back grain, the nations will curse him.'

phrases.english: '...the nations shall curse him,'
phrases.notes: This is the end of משלי 11:26, which opens with 'one who holds back בר'.

phrases.english: and לאום means only unborn babies,
as it says: 'And one nation shall be stronger than the other nation.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:23. ה׳ says this to רבקה about the twins in her womb.

phrases.english: And קבה means only a curse,
as it says: 'How can I curse whom God has not cursed?'
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:8, spoken by בלעם.

phrases.english: And בר means only Torah,
as it says: 'Kiss the בר, lest He be angry.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the פסוק that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who withholds תורה from a student is cursed even by unborn babies.

steps.title: A second reading: he is pierced like a sieve
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר ישמעאל reads יקבהו as 'pierce,' so the person who withholds תורה is punished by being riddled with holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר ישמעאל says: They pierce him like a sieve. It says here 'יקבהו לאום', and it says there 'And he bored [ויקב] a hole in its lid.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא בר ישמעאל gives a different meaning for the word יקבהו. He says it means piercing, not cursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a גזירה שוה-style comparison: the same root נקב appears in מלכים, where it clearly means boring a hole. So the punishment for withholding תורה is that the person is pierced full of holes like a sieve.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is written here... and it is written there': comparing the same word in two פסוקים

phrases.english: Ulla bar Yishmael says:
They pierce him like a sieve.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the one who holds back תורה from a student.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'the nations shall יקבהו him,'
and it is written there: 'And he bored a hole in its lid.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 12:10

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא בַּר יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: מְנַקְּבִין אוֹתוֹ כִּכְבָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different meaning for יקבהו than the 'curse' reading in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יקבהו means he is pierced like a sieve.

steps.title: אביי describes the kind of holes
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the holes are like those in a launderers' sprinkling tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: Like the sprinkler of the launderers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a picture to עולא בר ישמעאל's reading. He says what kind of holes the person is pierced with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue with עולא; he builds on him. He compares the holes to a launderers' tool full of holes used to sprinkle water on clothes, which makes the image sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: A perforated tool for sprinkling water

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
Like the sprinkler of the launderers.
phrases.notes: He means the person is pierced with holes like that tool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the image in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The piercing is like the holes of a launderers' sprinkler.

steps.title: What is the reward for teaching?
steps.stepSummary: After the punishment, the גמרא asks what reward a person gets if he does teach the student.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he taught him, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. Having learned the punishment for holding back תורה, it now asks about the reward for teaching it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the other side of the same פסוק. The first half talked about the one who withholds; the question now points us toward the second half, which talks about blessing.

phrases.english: And if he taught him, what is his reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment to the reward
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reward for one who teaches a student instead of withholding

steps.title: He gets blessings like יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב ששת, says the teacher receives blessings like יוסף, learned from the end of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב ששת: He merits blessings like יוסף, as it says: 'And blessing is on the head of the משביר.' And משביר means only יוסף, as it says: 'And יוסף was the ruler over the land; he was the משביר to all the people of the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Whoever teaches merits blessings like יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of משלי 11:26 says blessing comes to the משביר, the one who provides food. The same word is used for יוסף, who gave out grain in מצרים. So the teacher, who 'provides' תורה, gets blessings like יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: One who provides or sells grain

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק that warns against withholding תורה also promises blessing, like יוסף's, to the one who teaches it.

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
He merits blessings like Yosef,
as it says: 'And blessing is on the head of the provider.'
phrases.notes: The end of משלי 11:26, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: And משביר means only Yosef,
as it says: 'And Yosef was'
the ruler over the land, he was
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; they finish quoting the פסוק.

phrases.english: the provider for all the people of the land.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 42:6

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: זוֹכֶה לִבְרָכוֹת כְּיוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He merits blessings like יוסף, learned from the word משביר

steps.title: Teaching in this world, teaching in the next
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת teaches that whoever teaches תורה in this world will teach it in עולם הבא too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Anyone who teaches תורה in this world merits to teach it in עולם הבא, as it says: 'And he who satisfies others will himself be satisfied [יורה].'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds another reward for teaching תורה. The teacher will keep teaching in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the פסוק just before, משלי 11:25. He reads ומרוה as if it said 'מורה' (one who teaches), and יורה as 'he will teach.' So one who teaches now will also teach later.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching תורה is rewarded with blessing like יוסף's, and with the privilege of teaching in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Anyone who teaches Torah in this world
merits to teach it in the World to Come,
as it says: 'And he who satisfies others will himself be satisfied.'
phrases.notes: משלי 11:25. Mix up the letters of מרוה and you get מורה, 'teacher,' and יורה means 'he will teach.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה בְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reward for teaching, from the neighboring פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who teaches תורה in this world will teach it in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבא finds תחיית המתים in the blessing of ראובן
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where the תורה hints at תחיית המתים. He answers from משה's blessing to ראובן: 'live' in this world, 'and not die' in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Where do we see תחיית המתים in the תורה? From the פסוק 'Let ראובן live and not die.' 'Let ראובן live' means in this world, and 'not die' means in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new source from the חומש itself for תחיית המתים. He reads the two halves of one פסוק as two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'live' and 'not die' seem to say the same thing twice. רבא explains that they are not repeats. 'Live' is about this world, and 'not die' is about life again in עולם הבא, and that later life is תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do we know resurrection of the dead
from the Torah?
As it says: "Let Reuben live and not die."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:6

phrases.english: "Let Reuben live" means in this world,
"and not die" means in the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִנַּיִין לִתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the larger topic of finding a תורה source for תחיית המתים, after the side discussion about teaching תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double wording in 'יחי ראובן ואל ימות' points to life in this world and life again in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבינא brings a source from the book of דניאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a different פסוק: many who sleep in the dust will wake up, some to eternal life and some to shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said the source is from here: 'And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake up, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting disgrace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a second source for תחיית המתים. His פסוק says it openly: people sleeping in the dust will wake up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof needed a דרשה on two words. רבינא's פסוק says directly that the dead (those 'sleeping in the dust') will rise. It also adds that not everyone who rises gets the same result, since some rise to life and some to disgrace.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who sleep in the dust of the earth, meaning the dead

phrases.english: Ravina said: From here:
"And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awaken,
phrases.notes: דניאל 12:2

phrases.english: some to everlasting life,
and some to shame and everlasting disgrace."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same idea that רבא was proving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דניאל 12:2 openly says that those sleeping in the dust will wake up.

steps.title: רב אשי brings another source from דניאל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings the פסוק where דניאל is told he will rest and then stand up for his share at the end of days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said the source is from here: 'And you, go until the end, and you will rest, and you will rise up to your lot at the end of days.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third source for תחיית המתים. The פסוק speaks to one person, דניאל, telling him he will rest (die) and later rise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the פסוק teaches the point. First 'you will rest,' which means passing away. Only after that comes 'you will rise up … at the end of days.' Rising after resting is תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: And you will stand up to your share

steps.whatToRemember: Three אמוראים, three sources for תחיית המתים. רבא learns it from a דרשה on ראובן's blessing. רבינא and רב אשי bring clearer פסוקים from דניאל.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: From here:
"And you, go [until the end], and you will rest,
phrases.notes: דניאל 12:13. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and you will rise up to your lot at the end of days."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third source, alongside רבא and רבינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דניאל 12:13 describes resting first and rising afterward at the end of days.

steps.title: A gentle leader will lead his people in the World-to-Come
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a פרנס who leads the community calmly will merit to lead them in עולם הבא too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any leader who leads the community gently merits to lead them in the World-to-Come, as it says: 'For the One who has mercy on them will lead them, and by springs of water He will guide them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new saying. רבי אלעזר promises a calm, gentle leader that he will lead his people in עולם הבא as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof פסוק speaks of a merciful one who 'will lead them' and 'will guide them' by springs of water. רבי אלעזר reads it as a promise that the leader who leads with compassion now will go on leading them in עולם הבא. This is the same pattern as step 6: what you do here, you get to keep doing there.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who has mercy on them

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties to רב ששת's saying in step 6. In both, the reward in עולם הבא matches the good thing a person did in this world.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל פַּרְנָס שֶׁמַּנְהִיג אֶת הַצִּבּוּר בְּנַחַת,
phrases.english: Any leader who leads the community gently,
merits and leads them in the World-to-Come,
as it says: "For the one who has mercy on them will lead them,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:10

phrases.english: and by springs of water he will guide them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל פַּרְנָס שֶׁמַּנְהִיג אֶת הַצִּבּוּר בְּנַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new saying, linked to the earlier topic by the theme of reward in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leader who guides the community gently will lead them in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Knowledge is great because it sits between two names of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says דעה is great, since in the פסוק it appears between two names of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Great is knowledge, because it was placed between two 'letters' (names of ה׳), as it says: 'For a God of knowledge is ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another saying of רבי אלעזר. This one praises דעה (knowledge or understanding).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק 'כי אל דעות ה׳', the word 'דעות' stands between 'אל' and 'ה׳,' which are two names of ה׳. רבי אלעזר says that being set between two of ה׳'s names shows how important דעה is.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'two letters'; here, two names of ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two letters' here does not mean two letters of the alphabet. It means two names of ה׳ that stand on either side of the word.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: Great is knowledge,
for it was placed between two letters,
as it says: "For a God of knowledge is ה׳."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:3. Notice 'דעות' sits between two names of ה׳, 'אל' and 'ה׳'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another saying from the same speaker, רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דעה is great because the פסוק places it between two names of ה׳.

steps.title: The מקדש is great for the same reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses the same method to praise the מקדש, which also stands between two names of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Great is the Temple, because it was placed between two names of ה׳, as it says: 'You made, ה׳; the Temple, ה׳, Your hands established.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same 'between two names' method a second time, now for the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word 'מקדש' comes right between two times 'ה׳.' Because the method is now used twice, the next step can test whether it really works.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: Great is the Temple,
for it was placed between two letters,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״פָּעַלְתָּ ה׳ מִקְּדָשׁ ה׳ כּוֹנְנוּ יָדֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "You made, ה׳; the Temple, ה׳, Your hands established."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method as step 11, now applied to the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקדש is great because the פסוק places it between two names of ה׳.

steps.title: רב אדא challenges the method: what about vengeance?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא קרחינאה objects. If standing between two names of ה׳ makes something great, then נקמה (vengeance) would be great too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא קרחינאה challenged this: If so, then we should say vengeance is great, because it too was placed between two names of ה׳, as it is written: 'God of vengeance, ה׳, God of vengeance, shine forth!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא קרחינאה attacks רבי אלעזר's method. He shows that it seems to praise נקמה, which sounds like a strange thing to call great.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses רבי אלעזר's own rule. If 'between two names of ה׳' means 'great,' then the פסוק in תהלים, where 'נקמות' sits between 'אל' and 'ה׳,' would prove that vengeance is great. The question is whether the rule holds up or must be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so… (shows where your logic leads)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אדא is not saying that vengeance really is great. He is pointing out that רבי אלעזר's method seems to lead to an odd result. The גמרא's response comes in the lines right after this.

phrases.english: Rav Adda Karchina'a challenged it:
But if so, great is vengeance,
for it was placed between two letters,
as it is written: "God of vengeance, ה׳,
God of vengeance, shine forth!"
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:1

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא קַרְחִינָאָה: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method used in steps 11 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's rule that a word placed between two names of ה׳ shows that the thing is great.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule would make נקמה great, since in תהלים 94:1 it also stands between two names of ה׳, and that seems an unlikely thing to praise.

steps.title: Yes, in its own setting vengeance is great
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר accepts the point. In its proper context נקמה really is great, as עולא teaches: the two 'appearances' of ה׳ are one for good and one for punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In its own setting, yes, it really is so, like עולא said. עולא said: Why are there these two 'appearings'? One is for the attribute of good, and one is for the attribute of punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers רב אדא קרחינאה's challenge. He does not run away from it. He agrees that נקמה, in its proper place, is a great thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that calling נקמה 'great' must be absurd. רבי אלעזר says it is not absurd: when ה׳ takes vengeance on the enemies of the Jewish people, that is a real and great act of ה׳. עולא's teaching shows this, because ה׳ 'appeared' once in goodness and once in punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: In its own matter, meaning in its proper context
An appearing, when ה׳ shows Himself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as praising human revenge. The discussion is about ה׳'s vengeance against the enemies of the Jewish people, which ה׳ 'appeared' to carry out.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר answering רב אדא קרחינאה.

phrases.english: In its own matter, indeed it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: yes, in its proper setting vengeance really is great.

phrases.english: in line with what Ulla said.
For Ulla said:
These two 'appearings', why are they needed?
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are תהלים 94:1 ('appear!') and דברים 33:2 ('He appeared from Mount Paran').

phrases.english: One is for the attribute of good,
and one is for the attribute of punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by accepting it in context.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession in context: the challenge's 'absurd' result is accepted as true.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling נקמה 'great' seems wrong, so the method of 'between two names' would be broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: In its proper context, ה׳'s נקמה really is great, as shown by עולא's teaching about the 'appearance' for punishment.

steps.title: A person with understanding is like the Temple being built in his days
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person with דעה is as if the בית המקדש was built in his days, since both appear between two names of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has דעה, it is as if the בית המקדש was built in his days. This one was placed between two names, and that one was placed between two names.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר links his two earlier teachings together. Since both דעה and the בית המקדש stand between two names of ה׳, having דעה is like having the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 and 12 used the same method to call each of them great. Now רבי אלעזר says the shared pattern makes them equal. A person who has דעה has something as valuable as a בית המקדש built in his lifetime.

keyTerms.meaning: Letters; here it means names of ה׳

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any person who has knowledge,
it is as if the Temple was built in his days,
since this one was placed between two letters,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is דעה, and the 'letters' are the two names of ה׳ from steps 11 and 12.

phrases.english: and that one was placed between two letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֵּעָה, כְּאִילּוּ נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge is resolved, returns to the series of רבי אלעזר's teachings and joins steps 11 and 12 together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with דעה is like one in whose days the בית המקדש was built.

steps.title: A person with understanding will become wealthy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person with דעה will in the end become rich, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has דעה will in the end become wealthy, as it says: 'And by knowledge the rooms are filled with all precious and pleasant wealth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives another praise of דעה. A person who has it will eventually become rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching uses a direct פסוק, not the 'between two names' method. The פסוק says that through דעת rooms get filled with wealth, so the person with דעה ends up wealthy.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any person who has knowledge,
will in the end become wealthy,
as it is said:
'And by knowledge the rooms are filled'
phrases.notes: משלי 24:4

phrases.english: 'with all precious and pleasant wealth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֵּעָה, לְסוֹף מִתְעַשֵּׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same series by רבי אלעזר about דעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with דעה will eventually become wealthy.

steps.title: One may not have mercy on a person without understanding
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that it is forbidden to have mercy on a person who has no דעה, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has no דעה, it is forbidden to have mercy on him, as it says: 'For it is a people without understanding; therefore its Maker will not have mercy on it, and its Creator will not show it favor.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר now gives the flip side. He moves from praising people who have דעה to warning about people who lack it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that ה׳ does not have mercy on a people that lacks understanding. רבי אלעזר learns from this that people also may not show mercy to someone who has no דעה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to have mercy

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's series on דעה: it is great because it stands between two names of ה׳. It is like having the בית המקדש built in one's days. It brings wealth. And lacking it is so serious that one may not show mercy to such a person.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any person who has no knowledge,
it is forbidden to have mercy on him,
as it is said:
'For it is a people without understanding;'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:11

phrases.english: 'therefore its Maker will not have mercy on it,'
'and its Creator will not show it favor.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה אָסוּר לְרַחֵם עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series with the opposite case: a person who lacks דעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to have mercy on a person who has no דעה.

steps.title: Giving bread to someone without understanding brings suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that whoever gives his bread to a person without דעה will suffer. He reads the word מזור in a פסוק as meaning suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Whoever gives his bread to someone without understanding will have suffering come upon him. The פסוק says: 'Your bread they will make into a מזור under you; he has no understanding.' And מזור means suffering, because another פסוק says: 'אפרים saw his sickness, and יהודה his wound (מזורו).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another saying of רבי אלעזר about דעה: giving food to someone without understanding brings suffering on the giver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works in two stages. First, a פסוק links 'your bread' and 'no understanding' to a מזור. Then a second פסוק shows that מזור means a wound or suffering, because it is paired there with 'sickness.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן פִּיתּוֹ לְמִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה,
phrases.english: Anyone who gives his bread to one who has no understanding,
suffering comes upon him,
as it says: “Your bread, they will place a מזור under you,
phrases.notes: עובדיה 1:7

phrases.english: there is no understanding in him.”
And מזור means nothing other than suffering,
as it says: “And Ephraim saw his sickness,
phrases.notes: הושע 5:13

phrases.english: and Yehudah his wound (מזורו).”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן פִּיתּוֹ לְמִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's series about a person without דעה. After saying we may not pity him (Step 17), he adds that giving him bread brings suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever gives his bread to a person without דעה will suffer, based on reading מזור as suffering.

steps.title: A person without understanding ends up in exile
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person without דעה will in the end go into exile, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any person without understanding will in the end be exiled, as the פסוק says: 'Therefore My people went into exile, for lack of knowledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another short saying of רבי אלעזר: lacking דעה leads, in the end, to exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives exile as the result of 'lack of knowledge.' רבי אלעזר applies this to each person: whoever lacks דעה will be exiled.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה, לְסוֹף גּוֹלֶה,
phrases.english: Any person who has no understanding will in the end be exiled,
as it says: “Therefore My people went into exile, for lack of knowledge.”
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה, לְסוֹף גּוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another consequence of lacking דעה, in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person without דעה will in the end be exiled.

steps.title: A house with no תורה at night is burned by fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a house where no words of תורה are heard at night will be burned by fire. He reads the word שריד in the פסוק as a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any house where words of תורה are not heard at night will be burned by fire. The פסוק says: 'All darkness is hidden away for his treasures; a fire that no one fanned will burn him; it will go badly for the שריד in his tent.' And שריד means a תלמיד חכם, as it says: 'And among the שרידים whom ה׳ calls.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר moves from דעה to תורה learning. He says a home that is silent of תורה at night will be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'darkness' (night) and a fire that burns. 'It goes badly for the שריד in his tent' is read as: the house is harmed because no תלמיד חכם is learning there. A second פסוק proves that שריד means a תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: A survivor or remnant; here read as a תלמיד חכם

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any house in which words of Torah are not
heard in it at night,
fire consumes it,
as it says: “All darkness is hidden away for his treasures,
phrases.notes: איוב 20:26

phrases.english: a fire that was not fanned will consume him,
it will go badly for the שריד in his tent.”
שריד means nothing other than a Torah scholar,
as it says: “And among the שרידים whom God calls.”
phrases.notes: יואל 3:5

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל בַּיִת שֶׁאֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִשְׁמָעִים בּוֹ בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theme of lacking דעה to the theme of תורה learning, still within רבי אלעזר's series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house where no תורה is heard at night will be burned, based on reading שריד as a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: Someone who does not support תורה scholars never sees blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that whoever does not let תלמידי חכמים benefit from his property will never see a sign of blessing. Once again he reads שריד as תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Whoever does not let תלמידי חכמים benefit from his property will never see a sign of blessing. The פסוק says: 'There is no שריד to eat his food; therefore his good will not last.' And שריד means תלמידי חכמים, as it says: 'And among the שרידים whom ה׳ calls.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another saying of רבי אלעזר: if you do not share your wealth with תורה scholars, your wealth will not bring blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that because 'no שריד eats his food,' his good does not last. Using the same reading as the step before (שריד means a תלמיד חכם), this means that because no תלמיד חכם eats from his food, his wealth does not last. The גמרא repeats the proof for שריד because it is now being used for a new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets someone benefit, gives benefit to

steps.whatToRemember: Two of רבי אלעזר's teachings are built on one key: שריד means a תלמיד חכם. A house without תורה at night is burned, and wealth that does not support תלמידי חכמים does not bring blessing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְהַנֶּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִנְּכָסָיו,
phrases.english: Anyone who does not let Torah scholars benefit from his property
never sees a sign of blessing,
as it says: “There is no שריד to eat his food,
phrases.notes: איוב 20:21

phrases.english: therefore his good will not last.”
שריד means nothing other than Torah scholars,
as it says: “And among the שרידים whom God calls.”
phrases.notes: The same proof as in the last step, now used for a new teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְהַנֶּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִנְּכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reading of שריד as Step 20 for a new teaching about supporting תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever does not let תלמידי חכמים benefit from his property never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.title: Leave some bread on your table
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person who never leaves any bread on his table will never see a sign of blessing, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Anyone who does not leave bread over on his table will never see a sign of blessing, as it says: 'Nothing is left over from his food, therefore his good will not last.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי אלעזר: a person should leave some bread on the table after eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוק as cause and effect. Because nothing was left over from the meal, the person's good fortune does not last. So leaving bread over is linked to ongoing blessing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁיֵּיר פַּת עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who does not leave bread over on his table,
will never see a sign of blessing,
as it says: 'Nothing is left over from his food,'
phrases.notes: איוב 20:21. Here שריד simply means leftovers, not the תלמיד חכם reading from the last two teachings.

phrases.english: 'therefore his good will not last.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same series from רבי אלעזר, again built on the word שריד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who never leaves bread on his table will not see a sign of blessing.

steps.title: But leaving pieces of bread is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a clash. רבי אלעזר himself also said that leaving pieces of bread on the table is like עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: Anyone who leaves pieces of bread on his table is as if he worships idols, as it says: 'Who set a table for גד and fill mixed wine for מני'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last teaching. Another statement of רבי אלעזר seems to say the opposite, that leaving bread over is bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק from ישעיהו, people set a table for גד, an idol of luck. Leaving pieces of bread on the table looks like that idol practice. So which is it: is leaving bread good, or is it like עבודה זרה?

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (opens a contradiction)
name of an idol of good luck

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Anyone who leaves pieces of bread on his table
is as if he worships idols,
as it says: 'Who set a table for Gad'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 65:11. גד and מני are names of idols.

phrases.english: 'and fill mixed wine for Meni'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 22 with a statement from the same רבי אלעזר that seems to contradict it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's teaching that one should leave bread on the table.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rabbi says leaving pieces of bread is like עבודה זרה, so he seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: It depends on whether a whole loaf is there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no clash. One teaching speaks of a case where a whole loaf is on the table with the pieces, and the other of a case where there is no whole loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where there is a whole loaf with the pieces; that case is where there is no whole loaf with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by splitting it into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a whole loaf is already on the table, adding extra pieces looks like a setup for the idol גד, so that is the bad case. If no whole loaf is there, leaving some bread is the good practice that brings blessing. The two teachings are about two different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no real contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: Leaving bread on the table brings blessing. Leaving extra pieces next to a whole loaf looks like idol practice. The difference is whether a whole loaf is there.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא just says 'this' and 'that'. The idol worship case is the one WITH a whole loaf, and the good case is the one WITHOUT a whole loaf.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where there is a whole loaf with it,
phrases.notes: This is the idol worship case: pieces left next to a whole loaf.

phrases.english: that is where there is no whole loaf with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two different cases (הא בהא, הא בהא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings of רבי אלעזר seemed to clash about leaving bread on the table.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a whole loaf present, extra pieces look like idol practice. Without a whole loaf, leaving bread over is a good thing.

steps.title: Going back on your word is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that someone who changes his word is like an idol worshipper. He links the word 'מתעתע' said by יעקב to the word 'תעתעים' used about idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Anyone who changes his word is as if he worships idols. It is written here: 'And I will seem in his eyes like a deceiver,' and it is written there: 'They are nothing, a work of deceptions.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר about not keeping one's word or twisting the truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב worried that tricking his father would make him look like a 'מתעתע', a deceiver. ירמיהו calls idols 'תעתעים', deceptions. Because the same word is used in both places, רבי אלעזר says deceiving with your words is like serving idols.

keyTerms.meaning: one who changes his word, does not stand by what he said
it is written here... and it is written there (a word link between two פסוקים)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who changes his word
is as if he worships idols.
It is written here: 'And I will seem in his eyes like a deceiver,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 27:12. יעקב is worried about tricking יצחק.

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'They are nothing, a work of deceptions.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 10:15, speaking about idols.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the רבי אלעזר series. It picks up the theme of עבודה זרה from steps 23-24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who changes his word or deceives with his speech is like an idol worshipper.

steps.title: Staring at ערוה drains a man's strength
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person who looks at ערוה loses his strength. He reads a פסוק in חבקוק that plays on the sound of the word ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Anyone who looks at ערוה, his bow is emptied, as it says: 'Your bow will be made bare.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching from רבי אלעזר, this time about looking at what one should not look at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עריה' in the פסוק sounds like 'ערוה'. רבי אלעזר reads it as a hint: looking at ערוה causes one's 'bow' to be emptied. 'Bow' here stands for a man's strength.

keyTerms.meaning: nakedness, what one is forbidden to look at

steps.whatToRemember: This part of the גמרא is a list of רבי אלעזר's teachings. Each one ties a behavior to a result through a word in a פסוק.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who looks at nakedness,
his bow is emptied,
phrases.notes: 'Bow' is a way of talking about a man's strength.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Your bow will be made bare.'
phrases.notes: חבקוק 3:9. The word עריה sounds like ערוה, and that is the hint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate teaching in the רבי אלעזר series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who looks at ערוה loses his strength.

steps.title: Stay hidden and you will last
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר advises a person to always stay in the dark, out of the public eye, and then he will endure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Always stay in the dark, and you will last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more saying of רבי אלעזר: keep a low profile and you will survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list of רבי אלעזר's sayings from the earlier steps. The idea is that a person who stays out of the spotlight draws less attention and less harsh judgment, so he lasts longer.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Always be in the dark, and you will last.
phrases.notes: Being 'in the dark' here means staying low-key and out of the spotlight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another saying in the series of רבי אלעזר's teachings (steps 22-26).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who stays hidden and out of public view will endure.

steps.title: Support from the dark house with a possible נגע
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא shows that a משנה teaches the same idea: you do not open windows in a dark house to check its נגע, so it stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We have also learned this in a משנה: For a dark house, one does not open windows in order to see its נגע. Learn from it that this is true.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a משנה that supports רבי אלעזר's idea, and the גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house that is too dark to check for a נגע is left alone and stays טהור, because nobody opens windows to look. In the same way, something that stays hidden is left alone. 'שמע מינה' means the proof is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (in a משנה or ברייתא)
A צרעת mark (here, on a house)
Learn from it; the proof stands

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
We too have also learned this:
A dark house:
one does not open windows for it
in order to see its נגע.
phrases.notes: נגעים 2:3. Since nobody opens windows to check, the house stays טהור.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבי אלעזר's saying in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's saying that staying hidden lets a person endure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נגעים: windows are not opened in a dark house to check its נגע, so it keeps its טהרה.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק put the grave next to the womb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to תחיית המתים. רבי יאשיה asks why a פסוק in משלי lists the grave together with the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'The grave and the closed womb, the earth that is not filled with water'? What does the grave have to do with the womb?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main topic and sets up a question. Why does the פסוק put the grave and the womb side by side? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grave and the womb seem to have nothing in common. The question is a setup: putting them together in the פסוק must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
What does one thing have to do with the other?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The grave and the closed womb,
phrases.notes: משלי 30:16

phrases.english: the earth that is not filled with water"?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן שְׁאוֹל אֵצֶל רֶחֶם?
phrases.english: And what does the grave have to do with the womb?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the sayings of רבי אלעזר and goes back to sources for תחיית המתים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק places the grave next to the womb.

steps.title: The grave gives back, just like the womb
steps.stepSummary: The answer: just as a womb takes in and brings out, the grave also takes in and will bring out the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק is telling you: Just as the womb takes in and brings out, so too the grave takes in and brings out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the grave is like the womb because both take something in and later bring it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A womb receives a baby and later gives birth. Putting the grave next to it teaches that the grave also gives back what it received, which is תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is to tell you

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:
just as the womb takes in and brings out,
so too the grave takes in and brings out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grave and the womb are linked: both take in and bring out, so the dead will come out of the grave.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the womb to the grave
steps.stepSummary: A womb receives quietly and gives out with loud cries. The grave receives with loud crying, so surely it will give out with loud cries.
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't this a קל וחומר? A womb receives the baby in secret, yet the baby comes out with loud cries. The grave receives the dead with crying, so surely they will come out of it with loud cries!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the comparison even stronger by using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the womb, where things go in quietly, still brings out with great noise, then the grave, where things go in with loud mourning, should surely bring out with great noise. This adds strength to the idea that the grave will release the dead.

phrases.english: And are these matters not a קל וחומר?
If a womb, which things are put into in secret,
is still emptied with loud cries;
phrases.notes: He means the cries of the mother giving birth.

phrases.english: then the grave, which people are put into with loud crying,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין מִמֶּנּוּ בְּקוֹלֵי קוֹלוֹת?
phrases.english: isn't it logical that they will come out of it with loud cries?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the comparison from step 30 with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That the grave will give back the dead.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the womb, which goes in quietly and comes out with noise.

steps.title: An answer to those who deny תחיית המתים from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this derivation answers those who say תחיית המתים is not found in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here there is an answer to those who say: תחיית המתים is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: this reading of the פסוק answers people who deny that תחיית המתים has a source in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ending the derivation this way ties it back to the big question of the sugya: where do we see תחיית המתים in the written text? The link between the grave and the womb is offered as that kind of source.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead coming back to life

steps.whatToRemember: The grave is like a womb. It takes in and it will bring out, and with even more noise than a birth. This is a source for תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: From here there is an answer to those who say:
"תחיית המתים is not from the Torah."
phrases.notes: The פסוק used here is from משלי, so 'Torah' is being used broadly for the written text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the derivation in steps 29-31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק linking the grave and the womb answers those who deny a written source for תחיית המתים.

steps.title: The revived צדיקים will live forever
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו teaches that the צדיקים whom הקדוש ברוך הוא brings back to life will never return to dust, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of אליהו taught: The צדיקים whom הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring back to life do not go back to their dust, as it says: 'And whoever is left in ציון and whoever remains in ירושלים will be called holy, everyone who is written for life in ירושלים.' Just as the Holy One lasts forever, they too will last forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that after תחיית המתים, the צדיקים will not die again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls those who remain 'קדוש', which is a name of הקדוש ברוך הוא. Just as He lives forever, so will they.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring them back to life

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds that תחיית המתים is permanent for the צדיקים. They will not die again.

phrases.english: The school of Eliyahu taught:

phrases.aramaic: צַדִּיקִים שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחְיוֹתָן
phrases.english: The righteous whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring back to life
do not go back to their dust,
as it says:
"And whoever is left in Zion
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 4:3

phrases.english: and whoever remains in Jerusalem
will be called holy,
everyone who is written for life in Jerusalem."
Just as the Holy One lasts forever,
phrases.notes: Here 'קדוש' is read as a name of הקדוש ברוך הוא.

phrases.english: so too they will last forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of תחיית המתים and adds what happens to the revived צדיקים afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צדיקים who are revived will live forever and not return to dust.
